"Failure haven’t released an album since 1996, when Fantastic Planet dropped, and the band broke up a year later. This decade has wrought a series of revivals, as guitar-driven rock undergoes an unpredicted, though not unwelcome, renaissance of sorts."

Idk if anyone else here is a fan of Failure but IMO they are one of the MOST underrated bands of the 1990's. They were unfortunately eclipsed by Nirvana, and tormented internally by their own drug addiction problems But I would very much consider Failure "Musician's Musicians". They may not be very widely known by the mainstream music going public, but most rock bands of the era owe much inspiration from Failure. Their members, and music styles, went on to influence the likes of Queens of the Stone Age, A Perfect Circle, ON, Replicants, and many others.

I can't believe how good the new album "The Heart is a Monster" is. It is one of the best "comeback" albums I have EVER heard. Its like they never skipped a beat all the way back from 1996. I also think its great how they treated this album as a true spiritual successor to "Fantastic Planet", all the way down to the "Segue #" naming scheme of the filler segue tracks. Fantastic Planet had Segue 1, Segue 2 and Segue 3 scattered throughout the album, gluing it together. And so its a fan's wet dream that this new album began with track 1 named "Segue 4". SQUEEEEEEEEEEE

Has anyone else had a chance to really absorb this album? Any non-fans who were turned on to them by this? Any existing fans as blown away by this as me? Its pure gold, and easily my Rock Album of the Year 2015.

So basically...at first the sun light was different and there was only bacteria. The hole world was purple just like it is green today. Deep inside the water light was filtered and had less UV rays. Bacteria down there was green. Over time these dominated the waters of the world. The ancestor of all plants.

They would absorb light break down carbon into oxygen and hydrogen, and use the hydrogen to produce sugar and grow.

The first plants grew on rocks. Why? Because there was not as much dirt as there is today. As a matter of fact trees are responsible for most of the dirt we have today.

Trees would grow on rocks and destroy them as they grew creating tiny chunks of rock with plant waste...aka dirt. This also absorbed more water aka food for trees.

Then the plants started competing against each other. Growing taller and taller to catch more rays and expanding more and more. Until something awesome happened.

FUCKING LEAVES!!! They evolved to have leaves. And basically that is the reason why most plants look like Umbrellas and cast shade. They are trying to catch as much as possible.

Trees millions of years ago were so much different than today. Something insane happened then.

Too much oxygen. Double the levels of what we have today. So basically bugs, that are pretty basic organisms and have simple breathing tubes to inhale oxygen. So their size depends a lot on the levels of the oxygen. So bugs were massive back then.

There was a dragon fly whos wings spanned...10 meters! The biggest bug ever in the world.

So all is good and the Earth belongs to the plants until some fucking fish decide to start walk in the ground and grow 20 meters tall and start eating the plants.

So that is when they started becoming spicy, pointy and overall developing their own defenses.

I never knew plants could be so fucking awesome. But they are.
